subject: sociology
title: Methods & Methodology: Ethics & Theoretical Issues
welcome_lead: Good methods are honest, safe and reflexive.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology methods ethics BSA values value-freedom theoretical.
final_note: Ethics is not a checklist — it is ongoing judgement.

concepts.def: Participants understand and agree to research.
Weber — separate facts from values in research.

walkthroughs.body_html: The BSA Code: respect, transparency, no harm, informed consent, anonymity, honest reporting. Covert research is acceptable only when justified. Humphreys (1970) Tearoom Trade: classic ethics scandal — tracked anonymous sex contacts and visited their homes.

Weber (1949): research must distinguish facts from values. Gouldner (1962): total value-freedom is impossible — myth. Becker (1967) 'Whose Side Are We On?': researchers cannot avoid taking sides — usually with the powerful. Feminist methodology (Oakley) deliberately partisan.

Reflexivity: researchers reflect on their position (class, gender, ethnicity). Standpoint epistemology (Harding 1986): some views see society better — feminist standpoint, subaltern voices. Pre-registration and open data are recent transparency tools.
